clue.text: Boy, Lancelot's nephew, I included

indicators.note: something included is taken inside, so the nephew's name holds the other piece

parts.note: Sir Bors is a knight of the Round Table, kin of Lancelot
taken as written

explanation.surface: A genealogy note from Arthurian legend about a boy related to Sir Lancelot.
explanation.walkthrough: BOR(I)S: the Arthurian knight takes I in his middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris is a male first name, so a boy can be called it; a crossword-style name definition.

clue.text: Mark engaging in a witty conversation

indicators.note: to engage is to take hold of or enclose, so the mark wraps round the following words

parts.note: a badge is a distinguishing mark
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone named Mark joins in a sparkling exchange of wit.
explanation.walkthrough: BAD(INA)GE: 'Mark' reads as a man's name, but it is a badge holding IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is playful, teasing banter, which is exactly light and witty talk.

clue.text: Spot of rust on one? Check bolt

indicators.note: a spot is a tiny amount, so only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: first letter
the Roman numeral for one
to vet is to check or examine

explanation.surface: A maintenance inspector spots rust on a fixing and checks the bolt.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means R sits above I; then VET follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A rivet is a metal pin or bolt used to fasten plates together, so it serves as a kind of bolt.

clue.text: A director may have one to catch after ceremony

parts.note: a service is a religious ceremony
to contract an illness is to catch it

explanation.surface: A film director planning to film something right after a wedding ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the catching word behind the ceremony word. 'Director' is a company director, not a film-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A company director is typically employed under a service contract, the formal agreement setting out employment terms.

clue.text: Very close friends of bishop married, sporting very large gems

indicators.note: the gems are sporting, that is wearing, the married abbreviation within them

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
OS stands for outsize
opals are precious stones
M is the standard abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A newly married bishop and his friends, flaunting enormous jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: B + OS + O(M)PALS: the married abbreviation sits inside the gems, after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosom pals is an idiom for intimate companions, the bosom suggesting closeness to the heart.

clue.text: Finish ahead after run of successful pots

parts.note: in snooker a break is a sequence of balls potted in one visit
a team that is up is ahead

explanation.surface: A snooker player finishing the frame in the lead after a long run of pots.
explanation.walkthrough: Snooker, a cue game popular in Britain, calls a run of pots a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Schools break up for the holidays, and couples or meetings break up, meaning they end or disperse.

clue.text: Whip, for example, turned up, located after search

parts.note: to scour is to search thoroughly

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: the usual abbreviation for 'for example'

explanation.surface: A whip, say, that went missing and turned up after a search.
explanation.walkthrough: SCOUR + GE: 'located after' places the reversed abbreviation behind the search word.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a whip used for punishment, and to scourge is to flog.

clue.text: The study of social habits may suggest new movie star's a snob

indicators.note: something new is a fresh version, so these letters come out in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A sociological study might reveal that a fresh film star is a snob.
explanation.walkthrough: Mass-Observation was a British research project begun in 1937 that recorded everyday life and habits.
explanation.definitionFit: The project studied ordinary people's behaviour, and the term now names that kind of social survey.

clue.text: Finished in a group left behind

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the first word goes within the group

parts.note: a band is a musical group
done means finished

explanation.surface: A musician who has finished with a band and been left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: A BAN(DONE)D: the finished word goes inside A BAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abandoned has been deserted or left behind by its owner.

clue.text: Make a mistake having cast round for a drink

indicators.note: having something round you means it surrounds you, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to shy is to throw or cast; 'round' says it goes around
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone blunders by casting around for something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Shy is the old word for throw, as in a coconut shy at a fair; 'round' tells it to surround the mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine from Spain, so it is one kind of drink.

clue.text: I'd turned at the border to branch off

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so those letters are read backwards

parts.note: I'd without its apostrophe
a verge is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A traveller says they turned at the border to take a side road.
explanation.definitionFit: To diverge is to go off in a different direction, as roads separate at a fork.

clue.text: Performing animal is caged in one

indicators.note: a caged creature is shut inside something, so the animal sits within the other piece

parts.note: taken as written
a stag is a male deer

explanation.surface: A circus animal kept in a cage for its act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performing animal' reads as one phrase, but the definition is the single word 'Performing'.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who is on stage is in the middle of a performance in front of an audience.

clue.text: Note Italian, one who singles out fussy fault-finder

parts.note: N is an abbreviation for note
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it
a picker chooses or selects

explanation.surface: A note from an Italian who picks out the most pedantic critic.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitpicker is a pedant who obsesses over trivial errors, like picking nits from hair.

clue.text: Harmony in class

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a rank or category

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a quiet classroom; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Order means calm, regular arrangement and also a group or rank in a classification.

clue.text: Romantically entangled with a posh Chinese bird

indicators.note: something treated romantically is reimagined fancifully, so these letters are freely reshaped

parts.note: fodder
fodder

explanation.surface: Someone having an affair with an upper-class person from China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romantically entangled' reads as one phrase; only the first word signals the shuffle, and 'entangled' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden pheasant is a brilliantly coloured game bird native to the mountain forests of China.

clue.text: Poet getting praise in speech by King being broadcast

indicators.note: in speech means as spoken, so the word is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: to laud is to praise; in non-rhotic speech it sounds the same
taken as written
R for Rex, Latin for king
a programme that is on is being transmitted

explanation.surface: A poet being praised by a king in a broadcast speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being broadcast' looks like a second sound-alike signal, but it simply gives ON, as in on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Byron was a leading English Romantic poet, author of Don Juan.

clue.text: Fidgety? Be more active!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: unable to keep still

definitions.note: an instruction, read cryptically as two words
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an order to take less repose, split into two words

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads as a command split into two words: take less repose.
explanation.definitionFit: A restless person cannot settle or keep still, and telling someone to rest less urges more activity.

clue.text: New York: big blonde crossing river — here?

definitions.text: New York: big blonde crossing river — here?

indicators.note: new signals a fresh version, so the following letters are put into a fresh order

parts.note: fodder
fodder
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A tall blonde walking across a river in New York City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New York' looks like a single place name, but New is the shuffle signal; the whole clue also describes where the scene happens.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brooklyn Bridge is the famous New York suspension bridge on which a pedestrian crosses the East River.

clue.text: Light later round northern end of Britain

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the later word goes around the northern abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for northern

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so just that one is kept

parts.note: the last letter

explanation.surface: A beacon to be lit later around the far north of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: Two Ns are needed: the northern one goes inside, and Britain's last letter is tacked on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp, so it is a light in the sense of a source of illumination.

clue.text: Owner upset about horse that's lost heart, out of the running

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the word's letters are rearranged
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the remains of the horse

parts.note: the fodder letters, rearranged

indicators.note: losing the heart means the middle goes, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: the outer letters

explanation.surface: A racehorse owner is distressed because the dispirited horse is out of the race.
explanation.walkthrough: NOW(HE)RE: the horse loses its middle letters, leaving its first and last.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner who finishes nowhere is unplaced, so the idiom means having no chance of winning.

clue.text: Amtrac ruined road surface

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of shape, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: An amphibious military vehicle, an Amtrac, has churned up and wrecked the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarmac, tar-bound stone chippings, is the common paving material for roads and runways.

clue.text: Monastery head wants a couple of books on the Old Testament

parts.note: taken as written
B is an abbreviation for book, so two of them
the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: The head of a monastery asks for some Old Testament books to read.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbot is the superior in charge of an abbey or monastery of monks.

clue.text: Fashionable shopping centre in Suffolk town

parts.note: new things are the latest fashion
a market is a place for buying and selling

explanation.surface: A trendy new mall opening in a country town.
explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket, in the English county of Suffolk, is the home of British horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket is a market town in Suffolk, so the place name fits the definition directly.

clue.text: Pool equipment, extremely tacky

parts.note: kit is a set of equipment

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: the outer letters

explanation.surface: The gear at the swimming pool looks thoroughly cheap and nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pool' suggests swimming, but it means a shared fund of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitty is a shared pool of money that several people contribute to, as in card games.

clue.text: Damage barrier in resort town

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
a gate is a barrier across an opening

explanation.surface: Vandals have damaged a fence at a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Margate is a traditional seaside resort on the Kent coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Margate is a well-known seaside holiday destination, so it is a resort town by example.

clue.text: Long letter in pile set out

indicators.note: laid out means spread in a new layout, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A lengthy letter found in a pile of papers laid out on a desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' looks like the shuffle signal, but 'set' is fodder and only 'out' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal or lengthy letter, like the New Testament letters of Paul.

clue.text: Girl in European lake

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a female first name
second meaning: the lake bordered by Germany, Austria and Switzerland

explanation.surface: A girl swimming in a lake somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Lake Constance is the English name of the Bodensee.
explanation.definitionFit: Constance is a woman's name and also the English name of a large Alpine lake on the Rhine.

clue.text: Loud shouting, we hear, from English poet

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word is swapped for one with the same pronunciation

parts.note: loud shouting makes a din

explanation.surface: A loud racket heard coming from a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Noyes was an English poet best known for the ballad The Highwayman.
